title: POC Weekly Sync - Aurora Retail Closeout
summary: Final POC sync to review results from the 4-week pilot. Discussed latency/cost improvements from batching and quantization, model quality regression checks, stakeholder alignment on success criteria, and next steps for enterprise procurement and Dedicated capacity pricing.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-24
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Karen (Aurora Head of Data), Miguel (Eng Manager), Priya (Product), Ryan (CTO)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, juggling a few time zones so appreciate it. quick agenda, final results recap, any tuning notes, confirm success criteria met, and next steps for procurement and rollout. sound good?
[00:18] Karen (Aurora): yep sounds good, i'll be mostly listening but want to make sure we hit the accuracy thresholds we promised.
[00:30] Ethan (Redwood SE): quick note, i'm going to run through the numbers then open for questions. we pushed the tuned quantized v2 model plus KV caching and a small batching window. results are in the deck linked in chat.
[00:45] Miguel (Aurora): link came through, thanks. small heads up, we measured on our staging traffic shape, not full production spike profile.
[01:02] Ethan: understood, i'll call that out. okay results summary — latency median came down from ~120ms to ~78ms for 256 token median requests, 95th p90 is now ~185ms which meets your 200ms target, and cost per 1k tokens dropped ~22% vs baseline after batching and int8 quantization.
[01:27] Priya: those numbers look great. any degradation in classification accuracy? that's our primary success metric.
[01:34] Ethan: good question. classification F1 on the holdout set was 0.925 baseline, after quantization it's 0.919 — small delta, within the 0.03 tolerance we discussed. there were a couple of edge cases we flagged in the evals doc.
[01:55] Karen: ok 0.919 is fine if we can show the edge cases and acceptance criteria. can you point to examples?
[02:03] Ethan: yes, pushed a short examples sheet — key ones are long mixed-language product descriptions where tokenization differences change ground truth slightly. we also saw one vendor name aliasing issue.
[02:20] Miguel: are those things we can handle at the prompt layer or will require model change?
[02:26] Ethan: mostly prompt/template changes, plus a small pre-processing step for vendor alias normalization. that was part of the POC scope.
[02:35] Sofia: quick commercial note — since your latency and accuracy SLOs look satisfied, we should align on the purchase path: self-serve hosted vs Dedicated reserved capacity. Ryan, any preference from infra/cost perspective?
[02:48] Ryan (CTO): interested in Dedicated for predictable throughput and VPC isolation. also want KMS integration for keys and audit logs. we asked about SOC 2 docs earlier.
[02:59] Sofia: yes we'll send SOC 2 and full security pack after this. Dedicated gives you the reserved GPU pools, and we can set up a private control plane in your VPC. pricing is in the quote we'll share.
[03:12] Priya: timeline wise we have an executive review next Thursday, so can we get final numbers and an exec one‑pager by Tuesday?
[03:20] Sofia: yes we can do that.
[03:24] Ethan: back to technical items — we also tested auto-scaling with burst capacity for Black Friday traffic shapes, the autoscaler held with a cold-start median of ~850ms for an unprimed node but warm path stayed under 220ms.
[03:41] Miguel: 850ms cold start seems high, any mitigation?
[03:44] Ethan: we recommend priming strategies and keeping a small always-on pool for your peak windows; that's configurable in Dedicated. also KV cache warmup reduces token work for repeated sessions.
[04:02] Karen: on data retention and logs — we need 13 months of audit logs for compliance, is that doable?
[04:08] Sofia: yes that's an add-on for longer retention; we'll include options in the security/ops doc.
[04:16] Priya: can you confirm model pinning support? we need to freeze the serving model for the first 3 months.
[04:21] Ethan: yes, model pinning and rollout policies like canary/A-B are supported in the console.
[04:30] Sofia: i'll capture that in next steps.
[04:35] [05:00] (short cross talk about scheduling)
[05:20] Miguel: any issues around network egress costs if we go Dedicated in AWS in eu-west-1?
[05:27] Sofia: egress is priced by region, we'll provide an estimate; also we can do regional routing to minimize cross-region flows.
[05:40] Karen: one more risk — accuracy drift detection. We need alerting if F1 drops below 0.9 on daily evals.
[05:48] Ethan: we can wire up quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to your eval set, thresholds and slack hooks.
[06:00] Priya: great. can you confirm the exact datasets we used for the POC holdout?
[06:06] Ethan: holdout was 12k labeled SKU descriptions from your November export — names in the eval spreadsheet.
[06:12] Sofia: quick commercial recap — based on the numbers we propose a 6 month pilot-to-production path: 4 weeks of probation, then 6 weeks full pilot on Dedicated, then production commit. pricing will have a ramped reserved capacity discount.
[06:27] Ryan: for procurement we'll need an MSA and a data processing addendum. any standard templates?
[06:33] Sofia: yes we have templates, we'll attach them. legal can start review once you give lane.
[06:40] Ethan: small note on logs — we can ship audit logs to your SIEM or provide them via S3 for the retention period you need.
[06:50] Miguel: ok good.
[07:00] [07:20] Sofia: open to questions on the tuning results?
[07:25] Karen: you mentioned two edge cases — are they showstoppers?
[07:30] Ethan: not showstoppers; we marked them as medium severity and provided mitigation steps in the eval sheet.
[07:40] Priya: any end-user UX impact? we think latency improvements will help conversion on our checkout path.
[07:46] Ethan: based on prior benchmarks, sub-100ms median will reduce perceived latency, so should help cart completion.
[07:55] [08:10] (pause)
[08:30] Miguel: about the inference runtime — is the KV cache safe for PII? we need to ensure no customer PII is cached inadvertently.
[08:38] Ethan: KV cache can be configured to avoid storing PII, and you can enable scrubbing and tokenization rules before caching. we'll add config notes to the ops doc.
[08:52] Ryan: great. Security doc and SOC2, KMS, SAML all must be in the pack.
[09:00] Sofia: we'll include all that.
[09:10] Priya: do we have a tentative go/no-go checklist for execs?
[09:14] Sofia: yes — accuracy >= 0.915 on holdout, 95th p95 latency <200ms, cost per 1k tokens within budget (we'll put dollar numbers), and security controls in place.
[09:26] Karen: that matches what we discussed.
[09:30] Ethan: one more technical flag — when we roll to production we recommend enabling model replicas across multiple AZs to reduce downtime risk.
[09:40] Miguel: noted.
[09:44] [10:00] Sofia: ok let's capture next steps and action items.
[10:05] Sofia: next steps: 1) Sofia to send final POC report + deck + SOC2/security pack by Tuesday 2026-02-25 2) Ethan to publish eval examples and mitigation steps 3) Sofia to send Dedicated quote and pricing options 4) Schedule exec review for Thursday 2026-02-26 5) Legal templates attached for procurement.
[10:30] Priya: please include the simple one-pager for execs.
[10:40] Ryan: we may ask for a short live perf demo during exec review.
[10:45] Sofia: yes we can do that.
[11:00] Miguel: thanks all, sounds good.
[11:10] Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the exec review.
[44:30] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has minor transcription errors in product names (eg Redwood Dedicate), and occasional speaker label swaps in auto-export. Deck and eval spreadsheet referenced: https://redwood.example.com/aurora/poc-deck and https://redwood.example.com/aurora/evals
